relationships.subject: suzetrigine
relationships.evidence_quote: Suzetrigine inhibited human Nav1.8 currents with sub-nanomolar potency (IC50 ≈ 0.68 nM in human DRG; ~0.75 nM in monkey), while much less potent in rodents.

relationships.subject: Nav1.8
relationships.evidence_quote: Nav1.8 channels are found in the dorsal root ganglion (DRG) and are involved in mediating acute pain [13], Figure 1.

relationships.subject: suzetrigine
relationships.evidence_quote: Combined, these studies validate that suzetrigine effectively reduces nociceptor excitability via selective Nav1.8 blockade.

relationships.subject: suzetrigine
relationships.evidence_quote: Suzetrigine itself is a moderate inducer of CYP3A4, which may lead to reduced plasma levels of concurrently administered CYP3A4 substrates [20].

key_findings: Suzetrigine is a selective, allosteric Nav1.8 inhibitor (binds VSD2, closed-state preference) approved for moderate-to-severe acute pain without CNS or addiction signals in short-term trials.
Efficacy shown in bunionectomy and abdominoplasty but appears less potent than hydrocodone-acetaminophen; chronic pain efficacy untested.
